category: geocoding API and spreadsheet geocoder (US, Canada, Mexico)

free_tier.stated: Pay-As-You-Go plan: 2,500 lookups free per day, forever, for US, Canada and Mexico addresses; beyond that USD 1.00 per 1,000 lookups; 1 address or coordinate lookup is 1 credit and each additional data append is 1 more credit
free_tier.notes: no credit card is required until usage passes the free tier, and the overage is billed on the 1st of the following month instead of being refused; a billing limit can be set; the UK needs a Flex or Unlimited plan and Australia and New Zealand are outside Pay-As-You-Go

per_object_cap.stated: a batch request takes up to 10,000 lookups, each field append counting as a lookup; a CSV list job takes up to 1GB per CSV

retention.stated: data of spreadsheets processed through the lists API is deleted 72 hours after processing completes

egress.terms: not applicable: a query API metered in lookups, not bytes

interface_detail: HTTPS to api.geocod.io/v2 (GET /geocode and /reverse for one lookup, a POST of a JSON array for a batch of up to 10,000 lookups, and an asynchronous lists API for CSV, TSV and Excel files) with the key in an api_key parameter; spreadsheet geocoding is also in the dashboard; a keyless geocode answered HTTP 403 with Invalid API key
tooling: any HTTP client; spreadsheet geocoding in the web dashboard
chaining: 2,500 permanently storable lookups a day for US, Canada and Mexico addresses on an email account with no card, then USD 1.00 per 1,000; bulk work goes through batch requests of up to 10,000 lookups or CSV list jobs, each lookup costing 1 credit

limits.value: 2,500 lookups a day free on Pay-As-You-Go, then USD 1.00 per 1,000 lookups
1,000 lookups a minute on Pay-As-You-Go, answered with HTTP 429 beyond it
up to 10,000 lookups in one batch request; CSV lists up to 1GB per CSV

binding_note: 1,000 lookups a minute allows far more than 2,500 lookups in a day, so the free daily allowance is met first

identity_cost.detail: an account at dash.geocod.io with a name, an email address and a password, behind a terms checkbox; the page says no credit card is required, and a card is asked for only once usage passes the free 2,500 lookups a day

reliability_note: Pay-As-You-Go answers HTTP 429 at the 1,000-lookups-a-minute limit with X-RateLimit headers to read; a lookup past the free daily allowance is billed monthly, not refused
confidence_note: the pricing page, the FAQ, the storage terms, the API docs and the raw sign-up form were quoted on 2026-11-02; a keyless geocode answered HTTP 403. No account was opened, so the free daily allowance was not exercised.
